environment.webgl2: A real WebGL2 context rendered successfully in all three browsers, including WEBGL_lose_context restoration and WebGL handle tracking. This functional result does not establish hardware GPU performance for each browser. WebKit is Playwright WebKit, not a Safari device claim.

recheck.command: TEST_WORKERS=4 pnpm test:browser -- --phase=m5 --prepared --grep='real-worker races|two viewers|unavailable WebGL'
recheck.evidence: Actual observed Playwright JSON statistics and CLI completion: 9 passed (15.5s). The original .tmp/m5-browser.json was subsequently overwritten by the package reporter before archival; its per-round attachments are unavailable. This summary preserves the observed result and asserted conditions, and does not recreate the missing raw report or rerun tests to replace it.

reasons.resource: First-run resource checks reported a fixed 14 listeners. A single minimal create/load/dispose diagnostic per browser recorded every registration stack: 13 Playwright global/interceptor listeners and one externally injected AdGuard listener. Classification now follows concrete registration provenance; no constant is subtracted and every SDK listener must reach zero.
reasons.unavailable: The renderer error exposed code WEBGL2_UNAVAILABLE separately from its message. Error messages now include their diagnostic code; the original message assertion remained strict.
reasons.reviewCounterexample: The same affected asynchronous case gained a concrete visual-failure counterexample after review found a transient false-ready boundary: atomScale=Number.MAX_VALUE rejects while retaining the source, publishes no ready between computing and error, and atomScale=1 recovers. This is the sole scope expansion during the targeted recheck.
